argument: Nine words must read as one unstable sentence before they read as nine controls. Scale, spacing, broken syntax, and the pale sheet must carry the composition without interface chrome.

With readout, controls, hint, labels, and prose hidden, the first view must leave v047's strip, v048's witnesses, and v049's topology. It should read as language whose answer has been displaced, not a generic word grid or dashboard.

The visitor must approach a room and release, not click a target. Pointer, touch, keyboard, and deterministic control paths must offer equivalent meaningful routes; no hover-only action may carry the work.

A near relation is provisional. Only three distinct approach-and-release attentions can re-produce the sentence; a highlight, cursor, or status message cannot substitute for the false answer and global reflow.

The false word must land outside the attended trio, and all nine DOM tokens must change position, scale, weight, rotation, or word source. The model must answer from absence, not decorate the looked-at token.
Four misattributions must compound in one DOM field. Attention order must change the reflow, lift must reconstruct the exact previous sentence, and release must return to the quiet register.
Generated DOM spans, CSS custom properties, text reflow, and deterministic state are the medium. No screenshot, imported font, SVG, Canvas, or animal scene may carry the work.
little-critters is translated from situated reciprocal proximity into an absent-station answer. Animals, eyes, characters, paper, head-turning, source composition, and API surface are refused.

v050 changes representation, composition, encounter, temporal behavior, shape vocabulary, and viewer task: a browser-native sentence and absent-station misreading replace pressure, witnesses, and topology.

Delete v050 if proximity is only a highlight, repeated attention commits, the false answer lands in an attended room, only a local word changes, order is cosmetic, memory resets, exact lifting fails, or the blind field reads as a generic grid/interface.
